Article Title: Oil prices jump over 2% after US-Iran direct conflict re-ignites after a month of pause
Article Text:
Oil prices jump over 2% as Middle East tensions intensify

Oil prices rose more than 2% per barrel on Monday after conflict in the Middle East reignited once again with US attacking an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran hitting back at US bases in Jordan. Brent crude gained $1.86, or 2.11%, to $89.96 a barrel while WTI crude rose $1.60, or 1.92%, to $85.00 a barrel.Global benchmarks fell more than 4% last week, their first weekly decline in three weeks.The latest rise in oil prices came as the conflict in the Middle East continues to intensify. US forces struck two launchers on Iran's Larak island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first known US strike on Iran since late July.Iran responded by attacking two US air bases in Jordan, according to the Revolutionary Guards, cited by local media. Iranian state television later showed what it said were ballistic missiles being fired at the US bases in response to the American strikes.Jordan's armed forces said they intercepted eight missiles that entered the country's airspace early Monday. The latest exchange came as the conflict entered its sixth month.Talks to end the conflict are at an impasse, while mediators are working to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.A fifth of the world's oil flowed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war began at the end of February, keeping the waterway central to concerns over oil supplies as fighting intensifies.Shipping data showed that the number of visible commodity vessels sailing through the strait fell to five a day over the weekend, reflecting greater caution among companies.The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a tanker was hit by a projectile while sailing inbound through the strait on Saturday.The latest attack came days after the Trump administration said it would focus on economic pressure rather than military action to try to end the war with Iran.The plan includes threats to punish countries and entities that continue to do business with Tehran.The latest US strike came after Trump had said on August 1 that he would order the military to hold off on new strikes at the urging of Gulf allies Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.The last US military strike on Iran was confirmed on July 29, when Washington said it had carried out a “heavy wave of strikes” on dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets, including coastal surveillance and defence sites.Iran's Revolutionary Guard criticised Sunday's attack. Guard spokesperson Gen. Hossein Mohebi said in a statement carried by Iranian media that it was a “fatal mistake by the Trump regime during the economic war” and the enemy will pay the consequences militarily and economically.The US move towards sanctions came as the administration considers lower munitions stockpiles after months of war, raising concerns that a prolonged conflict could weaken US military readiness in other parts of the world.Meanwhile, Trump said on Sunday that oil from a recently struck deal with Venezuela would be used to refill the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has fallen close to its lowest level in 44 years.
Article Summary: Brent crude gained $1.86, or 2.11%, to $89.96 a barrel on Monday. WTI crude rose £1.60, or 1.92, to $85.00 a barrel. Global benchmarks fell more than 4% last week, their first weekly decline in three weeks.

Holding above Rs 153,000–150,000 could attract fresh buying interest, while a break below this zone may extend the correction towards Rs 145,000.

Article Title: ‘Losing $60 billion a year’: Trump slams Canada as ‘worst' trade 'abuser', urges firms to move to US
Article Text:
Trump's 50% tariff net caught 550+ Canadian goods

Trump slammed Canada while

US President Donald Trump has stepped up slamming Canada, claiming the US has been losing more than $60 billion a year in trade with its northern neighbour and saying Canadian businesses are returning to America to avoid tariffs while calling Ottawa a 'trade abuser'.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, "For many years, the USA has been losing more than 60 Billion Dollars a year with Canada. Why??? Our long ago stolen businesses are now coming back to America in order to avoid paying tariffs. They are lining up, just like the rest of the World!!!”Trump’s latest remarks came days after trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa broke down, further escalating tensions between the two countries.He has repeatedly singled out Canada over what he calls unfair trade practices and credited his tariff policies with reviving the US automotive industry.“When I announced that I was running in the 2024 Presidential Election, right at the beginning, Ford was getting ready to close their Big Factory, in Detroit. Then, because I was leading in the Polls, they figured they would leave it open a little longer to see what happened.Now it's running 24/7, and it's one of the most profitable Car Plants in the World!” Trump said in earlier post on Truth Social.He claimed there were “many other examples” involving Ford, General Motors and other companies, adding: “I've revived, and indeed saved, the Automobile Business in our America.”Trump attributed the turnaround to his tariff policies, saying, “That's because of what I've done with TARIFFS. One of the Worst Abusers is Canada. I don't want Canadian cars, I don't want Canadian parts, I don't want Canadian anything. They've been ripping us off for decades, and it's going to stop.”He also accused previous US administrations of failing to take a tougher approach towards Ottawa, adding, “This should have happened long ago with other Presidents, just as stopping Iran should have happened long ago.”Trump objected to what he described as Canada’s expectation of being treated like a US state. “They want to be treated like a State, but they aren't one. I deal with the Leadership of many Countries, but I find Canada to be the worst. They are entitled no longer!” he said.Trump has also urged Canadian businesses operating in the US market to relocate their operations across the border to escape tariffs. “Let all Canadian Companies that are doing business with America move to the United States, immediately."“Many of them are Companies that moved out years ago due to stupid US Leadership. When you move back, there are no TARIFFS!” he added.The latest escalation followed the collapse of US-Canada trade talks, after Washington imposed 50% tariffs on $27.6 billion worth of Canadian goods from August 22, covering products including steel, aluminium and other manufactured goods. Trump has also threatened to raise tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and auto parts to 50% from January 1, 2027.Canada is responding with 15%, 25% and 50% counter-tariffs on $27.6 billion of US imports from September 8, targeting products including steel and aluminium, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics and electronics.The latest measures deepen a trade fight that has already seen tariffs on autos, metals and other goods, putting pressure on the deeply integrated US-Canada supply chain and raising uncertainty around the USMCA trade agreement.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has stepped up slamming Canada, claiming the US has been losing more than $60 billion a year in trade with its northern neighbour. He said Canadian businesses are returning to America to avoid tariffs while calling Ottawa a 'trade abuser' Trump’s latest remarks came days after trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa broke down.

Article Title: India’s economy set for 7-7.2% growth in FY27 despite global headwinds: EY
Article Text:
India’s economy set for 7-7.2% growth in FY27 despite global headwinds

Industrial activity picks up pace

PMIs signals moderation

Capex push supports growth

Inflation remains a key risk

External sector faces headwinds

India’s economic engine is expected to stay firmly on track in FY27, with real GDP growth projected at 7-7.2%. The growth comes on the back of strong domestic demand and continued government spending on capital projects supporting economic activity, EY said in a recent report.The firm has pegged nominal GDP growth at 12.5-13%, saying that India's growth prospects remain relatively strong even as geopolitical uncertainty, high crude oil prices and a weaker global trade environment pose challenges.A stronger performance by the industrial sector has added to the growth outlook. India's Index of Industrial Production (IIP) expanded 7.3% in June 2026, its fastest pace in 23 months. Industrial growth averaged 5.7% during the first quarter of FY27, marking its strongest performance in eight quarters.Manufacturing was a key contributor, with output increasing 7.8%. Electrical equipment, motor vehicles, textiles and food products were among the better-performing segments.There are, however, signs that the pace of expansion may be moderating. Manufacturing PMI fell to 53.5 in July from 54.2 in June, while services PMI dropped to 53.3 from 57.4.Both remained above 50, indicating that the two sectors continued to expand.Credit conditions also remained supportive. Gross bank credit growth accelerated to 18.6% in June, its highest level in 25 months, EY said.Government spending is another key pillar of the outlook. Capital expenditure growth rebounded to 23.7% in the first quarter of FY27, reversing a 23.3% contraction in the fourth quarter of FY26. The fiscal deficit was at 18.2% of the annual budget target during the quarter.EY said the renewed push on capital expenditure should help sustain demand and strengthen the prospects for real GDP growth.Inflation, meanwhile, remains a key risk. Consumer price inflation was 4.4% in July, while wholesale price inflation stood at 9.8%, with mineral oils, food articles, metals, chemicals and fuels driving the increase.The higher WPI inflation could lift nominal GDP growth above the government's budget assumption of 10.04%, according to EY. This could support revenue receipts and enable the government to continue its capital expenditure push while maintaining its fiscal deficit target.The external sector could prove more challenging. Higher energy costs and weaker global demand may weigh on exports, while India's current account deficit could widen to 1.9% of GDP in FY27, based on OECD projections.EY said India could nevertheless improve its external position by reducing import dependence and increasing domestic value addition. A targeted approach covering 1,272 products could potentially replace around US$189 billion worth of imports.Alongside this, greater export promotion and domestic manufacturing could help reduce supply-side vulnerabilities over the medium term, the firm said.
Article Summary: India’s economic engine is expected to stay firmly on track in FY27, with real GDP growth projected at 7-7.2%. The growth comes on the back of strong domestic demand and continued government spending on capital projects supporting economic activity. A stronger performance by the industrial sector has added to the growth outlook.

Article Title: Rupee falls 13 paise to 95.56 as crude rises, Fed hike bets strengthen dollar
Article Text:
Rupee opens 13 paise weak against US dollar

Rupee started Monday on a weak note as higher crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions weighed down the currency, while growing expectations of a September US Fed rate hike boosted the dollar. Rupee opened at 95.56 against the US dollar at the interbank foreign exchange market, 13 paise lower than its previous close. It had ended Friday at 95.43, gaining 2 paise.Market participants have increased their bets on a September Fed rate hike, forex traders said. The resulting rise in US Treasury yields has supported a broad-based rally in the dollar, adding to the pressure on investor sentiment."The rupee opened lower as the dollar index was at 99.62 level, while most other assets fell from their levels on Friday," said Anil Kumar Bhansali, head of treasury and executive director Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.Bhansali expects limited movement in rupee through the session, with the currency likely to remain between 95.25 and 95.75."The rupee is expected to be in the range of 95.25 to 95.75 with exporters to sell near 95.60 levels and importers to buy all dips that they get with no directional movement being seen in the currencies," Bhansali added.The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was at 99.62, marginally lower by 0.07 per cent.Oil prices, meanwhile, moved higher amid renewed concerns over supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, climbed 1.34 per cent to $89.28 a barrel. The increase followed a renewed Middle East supply-risk premium after the US strike on Iran's Larak Island and subsequent Iranian retaliation, raising fresh concerns over oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.The Reserve Bank of India is intervening in the foreign exchange market to check any significant depreciation in the rupee, forex traders said. Sentiment also received some support from better-than-expected flows under the FCNR(B) scheme.Pressure was also visible in domestic equities, with Sensex falling 226.60 points to 77,028.56 and Nifty declining 120.40 points to 24,053.55 in opening trade.Foreign institutional investors had sold equities worth Rs 5,039.80 crore on a net basis on Friday, according to exchange data.Rupee's movement comes even as India's foreign exchange reserves reached a record high. The country's reserves rose by $12.422 billion to $729.328 billion in the week ended August 21, the RBI said on Friday.Meanwhile, the focus on India-US trade is set to continue, with the commerce ministry scheduled to meet industry associations and representatives of export promotion councils on September 1 to discuss India-US trade performance.The meeting will be chaired by commerce ministry additional secretary Darpan Jain, who is also India's chief negotiator for the India-US bilateral trade agreement.
Article Summary: Rupee opened at 95.56 against the US dollar at the interbank foreign exchange market, 13 paise lower than its previous close. Market participants have increased their bets on a September Fed rate hike, forex traders said. The resulting rise in US Treasury yields has supported a broad-based rally in the dollar.

Article Title: HDFC Bank shares rise nearly 3% after CEO Jagdishan opts out of reappointment
Article Text:
Jagdishan is serving his second three-year term as the lender's head

Shares of HDFC Bank climbed nearly 3 per cent on Monday, bucking a weak broader market, after MD and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan announced his decision to not seek reappointment when his current term ends on October 26.The stock gained 2.70 per cent to Rs 739.50 on the BSE and 2.70 per cent to Rs 739.75 on the NSE. The gains came despite the Sensex falling 464.66 points and the Nifty declining 174.60 points during morning trade.Jagdishan, 61, will retire from HDFC Bank after nearly three decades with the lender. He took over as CEO in October 2020 and is currently serving his second three-year term.HDFC Bank said its board will fast-track the selection and appointment of his successor “well within time”. Jagdishan had reiterated his decision not to seek another term despite “persuasion” from the board, as quoted by PTI.The bank’s board “deeply appreciated his commitment, leadership, contribution to the growth and stability of the Bank” and his role in the successful completion of the HDFC merger.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank's stock gained 2.70 per cent to Rs 739.50 on the BSE. The gains came despite the Sensex falling 464.66 points and the Nifty declining 174.60 points. Jagdishan, 61, will retire from HDFC Bank after nearly three decades.

Article Title: Milk gets costlier: Tamil Nadu raises procurement price; wholesale prices in Mumbai to cross Rs 100
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu raised its milk procurement price by Rs 3 per litre and Mumbai’s wholesale price by Rs 9 per litre.

Milk prices are set to rise in Tamil Nadu and Mumbai, with dairy producers citing higher cattle feed, transport and maintenance costs. .Tamil Nadu recorded a Rs 6 per litre cumulative hike in milk procurement prices in less than two weeks, while Mumbai is set for a Rs 9 per litre increase in wholesale rates from September 1, according to ANI.In Tamil Nadu, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced a Rs 3 per litre increase in Aavin’s milk procurement price, raising it from Rs 41 to Rs 44 per litre. The hike will cost the state government an additional Rs 60 crore a month, or Rs 720 crore annually, and comes less than two weeks after the procurement rate was raised from Rs 38 to Rs 41 per litre.Meanwhile, in Mumbai, the Bombay Milk Producers Association has announced a Rs 9 per litre increase in wholesale milk prices from September 1. The rate will rise from Rs 93 to Rs 102 per litre and remain in effect until February 28, 2027.Dairy farmers and cattle shed operators in the Mumbai region have attributed the hike to rising costs of green fodder, grain husks and oil cakes, along with higher transportation and livestock maintenance expenses. The Mumbai wholesale increase is expected to push up retail milk prices and raise costs for dairy products such as curd, paneer and sweets, particularly ahead of the festive season.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu recorded a Rs 6 per litre cumulative hike in milk procurement prices in less than two weeks. Mumbai is set for a Rs 9 per litres increase in wholesale rates from September 1. Hike will cost the state government an additional Rs 60 crore a month, or Rs 720 crore annually.

Article Title: Zomatao to de-list dishes with analogue dairy products
Article Text:
Zomato has announced a zero-tolerance policy on the sale of analogue dairy dishes by restaurants listed on its platform.

MUMBAI: Zomato has announced a zero-tolerance policy on the sale of analogue dairy dishes by restaurants listed on its platform, with immediate effect delisting dishes that restaurant partners have declared as containing analogue dairy.Under the policy, restaurants must transition to natural dairy products or remove items containing analogue dairy from their menus if an immediate transition is not feasible. They must also review product labels and ingredient declarations provided by suppliers to verify the ingredients used and ensure accurate representation of products listed on the platform.Restaurants that remain non-compliant will be delisted. Zomato said the policy is part of its focus on food quality, transparency and healthier food choices for customers, consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.According to Aditya Mangla, CEO, Zomato, the policy is aimed at safeguarding customer health and maintaining clear standards for products listed and served by restaurant partners. "This policy reflects that commitment, one we're taking together with partners who share it," he said.
Article Summary: Zomato has announced a zero-tolerance policy on the sale of analogue dairy dishes by restaurants listed on its platform. Restaurants must transition to natural dairy products or remove items containing analogue dairy from their menus. Zomato said the policy is part of its focus on food quality, transparency and healthier food choices.

The conversation has now shifted from why invest in India to how much more to invest. The internal discussion in Japanese boards is moving from assembling in India for the local market to making in India and making for the world.We have been in India for a long time and there are a lot of investors who invest through us. We are owned 75% by Nippon and from our point of view repatriation of dividends has been smooth.There is a lot of political and policy certainty in India now. Since Mr Modi became PM, Japan has seen five or six PMs. At the roundtable with foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), the sentiment was very strong.After FDI, we are going to see more Japanese portfolio flows. Japan has a savings pool of $14 trillion, of which half is in bank accounts. Of the asset management money of $2.2 trillion, one-third, which is around $800 billion, is invested overseas and India gets around 1% of that. Now, more household money will come to India. Through NISA, Japanese govt is trying to encourage more overseas investment and Nippon just launched a scheme for that.India is world’s fastest growing economy it offers tremendous returns. It always starts with FDI, which is followed by FPI and then retail. We have funds focused on different categories of Japanese investors and there is a very positive trend of AUM and flows of India-focused funds in Japan: from $6.7 billion in 2016 to $9.7 billion in 2021 and $19.6 billion in 2026.One or two months do not affect the overall trend. New investors have been coming into the market; new SIPs were opened and gross inflows remained positive. Investors have matured, during times when markets are choppy, they invest lumpsum, otherwise, they prefer SIPs.Crude prices have an impact on import bills and current account deficit, which impacts the rupee. The FCNR(B) initiative has been very successful. FPI inflows have turned positive after outflows for a few months, and the rupee seems to have stabilised. So, things are falling in line.It is a step in the right direction as it seeks to build transparency into the system. Any structural change takes time to settle and things will get better. It will help mutual funds in better price discovery, which is good for NAV and reduces tracking error differences in passive funds.
Article Summary: Nippon Life India Asset Management Company MD & CEO Sandeep Sikka was part of a 200-member business delegation that accompanied commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal to Japan. Sikka argues that there will be a rush of investments from Japan, with FDI translating into higher portfolio flows.

Article Title: Despite global headwinds, Q1 growth seen resilient on demand, government capex
Article Text:
Economists estimate Q1 GDP growth at 7-7.5%, supported by consumer spending, govt capex and manufacturing.

NEW DELHI: Despite facing significant headwinds from late onset of southwest monsoon and geopolitical uncertainties caused by lingering conflict in West Asia and uncertain tariff policies, growth momentum in April-June quarter is likely to have held up — aided by consumer spending, govt capex, robust growth in exports, along with manufacturing and construction sectors.Economists reckon gross domestic product (GDP) likely grew 7- 7.5% in Q1 FY2026-27, a tad slower than 7.8% in Q4 of 2025-26, though higher than 6.8% recorded in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. In its latest monetary policy review earlier this month, RBI pegged June quarter growth at 7%.The National Statistical Office (NSO) is scheduled to release official GDP data for Q1 on Monday.However, economists anticipate a slight moderation in growth during subsequent quarters due to high base effect and the renewed hostilities in the Iran -US conflict, which could affect energy prices and corporate margins .HDFC Bank principal economist Sakshi Gupta expects Q1 headline print at 7.5% and nominal growth to cross 13%, as manufacturing and electricity propelled industrial growth, while the pass through effect of income tax and GST rate cuts sustained consumer spending on the demand side. “Quarterly earnings results showed the impact on profit margins due to higher input costs has been partly offset by higher volume sales with strong net sales in auto, consumer durables and power,” she added.DBS Bank senior economist Radhika Rao said high frequency indicators in Q1 suggest that the economy weathered geopolitical disruptions “better” than initially feared and clocked 7.5% growth. “Industrial activity accelerated, although demand for industrial fuels and downstream petroleum products remained soft following price adjustments.” Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis moderates growth expectations to 7% in Q1 as delayed monsoon, lower reservoir levels and aggravated heatwave conditions are likely to pull agricultural growth lower (3.5%) than 4.4% in Q1 of 2025-26. Although, agriculture growth is expected to pick up in the coming quarters.ICRA Ratings chief economist Aditi Nayar also expects growth to cool down to 7% in Q1 as profit growth of a large group of non-finance companies slowed vis - a vis Q4 FY2025-26, amid sizable losses experienced by oil companies.“The gross value added in services sector is expected to have slowed down, amid a broad - based deceleration across all sub -sectors,” she added.
Article Summary: Economists reckon gross domestic product (GDP) likely grew 7-7.5% in Q1 FY2026-27. In its latest monetary policy review earlier this month, RBI pegged June quarter growth at 7%. National Statistical Office (NSO) is scheduled to release official GDP data for Q1 on Monday.

Article Title: Flood fears in Bihar as several rivers cross danger marks amid Nepal rains
Article Text:
Gandak river has crossed the danger mark in Gopalganj, while the barrage at Valmikinagar released around 99,800 cusecs of water at 8 pm on Saturday.

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you satisfied with the current response from government officials regarding the flood situation? Yes, very satisfied No, not satisfied 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With agency inputs)





PATNA: Flood fears intensified in Bihar on Saturday as persistent rains in Nepal and the state caused water levels in several rivers to rise above danger marks.The rivers were already swollen following flash floods in the neighbouring Himalayan nation earlier this week.According to the Water Resources Department, the Gandak river has crossed the danger mark in Gopalganj, while the barrage at Valmikinagar released around 99,800 cusecs of water at 8 pm on Saturday.Wednesday’s flash flood in Nepal, triggered by an ice-rock landslide, has prompted the administrations in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to intensify monitoring of river systems downstream of the Himalayan rivers."The water level of several rivers, including the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and the Ganga, has been rising. Incessant rainfall in the catchment areas of Nepal has led to rivers touching or flowing above the danger level at several places," a senior official of the Water Resources Department told news agency PTI on Saturday.The Kosi and Burhi Gandak rivers have reached the danger level in Khagaria, Katihar and Kursela, while the Ganga is flowing above the danger mark at Hathidah and Gandhighat in Patna, as well as Kahlgaon in Bhagalpur, according to a Water Resources Department bulletin.People residing in low-lying areas have been moved to safety, said a senior official, adding that all departments concerned have been put on alert."District magistrates have been directed to monitor the situation personally. Flood Control Department officials and engineers are camping at certain vulnerable sites in Bhagalpur, Purnea, Katihar, West Champaran and other districts," the official said.
